desc:
Email parsing for orders and requests reads each new message and saves the details you need to a sheet, CRM or order tool. Ecom Swift LLC connects to the inbox you choose and labels anything that does not fit, so no email is lost.

## What is email parsing?

Email parsing is the automatic reading of incoming messages to find specific details, such as a customer name, phone number, product, quantity, delivery date or requested service. The details are written into a structured place: a row in a sheet, a record in a CRM or an order in your system. The email itself stays in the inbox.

It is useful wherever people send free-text requests instead of filling in a form, which is very common for small businesses that take orders or enquiries by email.

## Why copying details out of emails goes wrong

When an order arrives as a paragraph, someone has to read it, find the facts and retype them. At a busy hour, that step is the one that gets delayed. A phone number is mistyped, a date is read as the wrong month, a second attachment is missed. The customer notices when the wrong item turns up.

The work is repetitive, so it is also tedious, and tedious work is where attention drifts. Meanwhile, the same facts must often be entered in two or three places, which multiplies the chance of a mismatch.

## How faster intake improves response and accuracy

Parsing moves the first stage of intake out of a person's day. New orders and requests appear in your sheet or tool within moments, in consistent columns, ready to act on. Your team starts from a clean record rather than a raw message, and replies sooner.

Confirmation emails to senders can tell customers their request was received, which cuts follow-up questions. A daily summary can show the team what arrived overnight. The results depend on how regular your emails are: a standard order email is easy to read, while a long rambling message may need a person. We design for that by leaving doubtful emails labelled in the inbox.

## What a good parsing set-up includes

- A connection to one inbox, shared mailbox or address, set up with read access you control.
- A defined list of email types, such as order, quote request or booking.
- A defined list of details to capture from each type, with a name and format for every one.
- Handling of attachments, saved to a folder and linked in the record.
- Results written to a sheet, CRM or order tool with consistent column names.
- A label on every email that did not match, so you can find it at once.
- Optional automatic confirmation to the sender, with wording you approve.
- An optional daily summary sent to your team.
- A test on past emails before the flow goes live.

## How we build it

We start by reading a set of your real emails and sorting them into types. For each type, we list the facts you need and how they usually appear: in a subject line, a signature, a table or a plain sentence. You confirm the list.

Then we build the reader, connect it to your inbox and test it against past messages, comparing every captured detail with what a person would have written down. The Basic package covers one inbox, one email type and a modest list of details sent to a sheet. Standard handles several email types, a CRM or order tool, labels for unmatched emails and saved attachments. Premium adds a larger set of details, confirmation messages, a daily summary and a test on a hundred past emails.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share examples of both tidy and messy emails for each type.
- Decide which details are essential and which are only nice to have.
- Keep a person responsible for the unmatched label.
- Ask customers to use a short template where you can, to make reading easier.
- Review the first week of results against the inbox.

**Avoid:**
- Letting the flow reply to customers with wording you have not approved.
- Capturing every possible detail when only a few are used.
- Forgetting to tell the team where results now appear.
- Using one flow for emails that are really very different in kind.
- Treating a parsed order as final before the checks you choose have passed.

## Who this service is for

It suits a catering or wholesale business that receives orders by email each morning. It suits a services firm whose enquiries arrive through a contact address and need to reach a CRM. It also suits a property or travel business where booking details come in free-text messages and must reach a calendar or sheet.

## What we need from you

Please send a sample of past emails, the list of details you want, and a note on where each detail should go. We need to know which inbox is involved and who can approve the connection. We never need your password. Mailboxes are connected through the sign-in and permission screens your email provider offers, or through a delegated or team user, and you can revoke that access whenever you wish.
